intervention_label: Comprehensive genomic profiling — paired DNA + RNA fusion NGS (with MSI/TMB) plus HER2 IHC with reflex ISH and MMR IHC
expected_benefit: Resolves seven of eight candidate axes in one pass; roughly 40% pretest chance of an actionable alteration that opens FDA-approved second-line therapy.
key_risks: DNA-only panels miss a subset of FGFR2 fusions with intronic/novel breakpoints — RNA arm required
HER2 and dMMR need protein/ISH readouts (4B5 IHC, MMR IHC), not an NGS copy-number or MSI score alone
2-3 week turnaround delays therapy start; archival RNA quality can degrade
preference_alignment: matches prefers_trials: YES (gate for every downstream trial); no toxicity veto to clear; no modality constraint. Balanced 0.5 weight served without tension.
guideline_status: NCCN Biliary Tract Cancers v2.2025 advises CGP at diagnosis of unresectable/metastatic disease.
rationale_summary: Every candidate feature is ngs_pending, so the confirmatory test is itself the first action and every therapeutic row below is gated on it. All five personas ranked this first: a paired DNA+RNA panel carries no toxicity and resolves the FGFR2, IDH1, BRAF, KRAS, NTRK and RET axes at once, while HER2 IHC with reflex ISH and MMR IHC close the two axes NGS copy-number cannot. The conservative, critic, and advocate each insisted the RNA fusion arm be in the order because DNA-only calling misses FGFR2 fusions with odd breakpoints, the highest-yield axis in this disease. A clean negative sends the patient to standard chemotherapy, which is the treating team's path and outside this ranking's scope.
open_questions: Tumor subsite (intrahepatic vs extrahepatic/gallbladder) is unspecified and shifts the prior for each axis
Whether archival tissue is adequate for RNA or a ctDNA parallel is needed
likelihood_of_effect: Diagnostic certainty — resolves which feature-conditional pathway is reachable; ~40% prior probability of a targetable hit across the panel (NCCN CGP guidance).
overall: The gate every therapeutic option depends on — non-toxic, unanimously first-ranked, and the only action available while all eight axes read unmeasured.

intervention_label: Ivosidenib (if IDH1 R132 confirmed on tumor NGS)
expected_benefit: ClarIDHy PFS HR 0.37 (95% CI 0.25-0.54, p<0.0001), mPFS 2.7 vs 1.4 mo; ORR 2% — delayed progression, not shrinkage.
key_risks: QT prolongation (class effect; one grade 3) — baseline and on-treatment ECGs
Serious AE 30% vs 22% placebo; no treatment-related deaths
preference_alignment: matches balanced 0.5 weight: oral, near-placebo grade 3+ profile, only randomized evidence in the set; serves prefers_trials via NCT02989857. No veto to clear.
guideline_status: NCCN Biliary Tract Cancers v2.2025 category 1 (the only category-1 anchor in the set); ESMO 2024 interim update recommends after >=1 prior line (MCBS v1.1 score 2).
rationale_summary: This is the only randomized phase 3 in the dossier and now the sole NCCN category-1 anchor, which is why the consensus places it first among the biomarker-conditional therapeutics despite a thin effect size. The honest reading, which the critic sharpened and the concensusite conceded, is that the category-1 grade rests on the PFS win (HR 0.37): the intention-to-treat OS did not separate at alpha (HR 0.69, p=0.060), and the 0.46 figure is an RPSFT crossover adjustment after 70% of placebo patients crossed over, a sensitivity model rather than the trial's survival result. ORR was 2%, so the realistic goal is disease control and tolerability, not shrinkage. The risktaker, weighting magnitude, placed it last on its own board but did not dissent from its inclusion; no persona vetoed it. IDH1 R132 runs 15-20% in intrahepatic CCA, so a positive call is one of the likelier returns.
open_questions: IDH2 and non-R132 IDH1 variants do not qualify — panel must cover the exact hotspot
Whether an ivosidenib-plus-checkpoint trial adds to single-agent control (preclinical IFNγ-TET2 immunoevasion mechanism, pmid:34848557)
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate for control, low for shrinkage: randomized PFS HR 0.37 (pmid:32416072) but ORR only 2% and ITT OS non-significant (HR 0.69, p=0.060).
toxicity_burden: Low (ascites 7%, QT prolongation, fatigue — grade 3+ tracked placebo)

counter_productive_moa.description: No counter-productive vector; risktaker's dissent was magnitude-of-benefit, not mechanism.

overall: The only randomized and only category-1 option, but the survival claim rests on a PFS win and crossover modeling — buys control, not response.
scenario_label: If IDH1 R132 confirmed on tumor DNA NGS

expected_benefit: FOENIX-CCA2 ORR 42% (95% CI 32-52), mDoR 9.7 mo, mPFS 9.0 mo, mOS 21.7 mo; only 2% discontinued for toxicity.
preference_alignment: matches balanced 0.5 weight: oral, on-label, durable; no veto. Higher grade-3 hyperphosphatemia than pemigatinib is a within-lane tradeoff, not a veto trigger.
guideline_status: NCCN Biliary Tract Cancers v2.2025 category 2A; ESMO 2024 backs the FGFR-inhibitor class after one prior line (MCBS v1.1 score 3, scored on the class).
rationale_summary: FGFR2 fusion is the highest-yield axis at 10-15% of intrahepatic CCA, and futibatinib is the peer-reviewed, on-label anchor of that lane. The critic ranked it ahead of the FGFR2-selective agents precisely because FOENIX-CCA2 is published NEJM data and its covalent chemistry holds against several post-pemigatinib kinase-domain resistance mutations — a sequencing fact the board could stand on rather than extrapolate. The concensusite and advocate edge it above pemigatinib on that resistance coverage plus a slightly higher response rate; the conservative dissents on order within the lane, defaulting to pemigatinib on its milder grade-3 hyperphosphatemia distribution and longer post-approval record. That is a within-lane sequencing disagreement, not a dissent against futibatinib itself, and no veto was issued. The registered endpoint is a surrogate ORR with no randomized comparator, which caps confidence below ivosidenib's RCT pedigree.
open_questions: Eligibility was built on intrahepatic CCA; a non-intrahepatic subsite weakens the match
Optimal FGFR sequencing (futibatinib first vs after pemigatinib progression) is not settled by head-to-head data
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate-to-high in FGFR2-fusion disease: ORR 42%, mOS 21.7 mo (pmid:36652354), concordant in direction with FIGHT-202 and the selective agents.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (hyperphosphatemia 30% G3+, AST rise, stomatitis, fatigue)

counter_productive_moa.description: On-target FGFR inhibition; acquired kinase-domain resistance blunts durability but covalent binding delays escape.

overall: The published, on-label FGFR2 anchor with a resistance-coverage edge for sequencing; response is a surrogate endpoint with no randomized comparator.
scenario_label: If FGFR2 fusion/rearrangement confirmed (RNA-based fusion panel preferred)

expected_benefit: FIGHT-202 ORR 35.5% (95% CI 26.5-45.4), mDoR 7.5 mo, mPFS 6.9 mo; first FGFR inhibitor approved in CCA with a companion diagnostic.
key_risks: Hyperphosphatemia 55% any grade (no grade 3-4); hypophosphatemia grade 3+ 12%
Serous retinal detachment 4% (one grade 3) — scheduled ophthalmologic monitoring
preference_alignment: matches balanced 0.5 weight: oral, on-label, longest post-approval safety record. Conservative's preferred FGFR2 first-line choice on grade-3 tolerability. No veto.
guideline_status: NCCN Biliary Tract Cancers v2.2025 category 2A; ESMO 2024 FGFR-inhibitor class MCBS v1.1 score 3.
rationale_summary: Pemigatinib is the other guideline-endorsed FGFR2 option and the conservative persona's lead FGFR pick, favored on the depth of post-approval follow-up and a milder grade-3 hyperphosphatemia distribution than futibatinib (55% any grade, no grade 3-4). It ranks just below futibatinib because the sequencing edge on kinase-domain resistance runs the other way, so once the fusion confirms this is a within-lane call rather than a hierarchy. Two independent single-arm trials converging on the same fusion axis is what gives the FGFR recommendation its footing. Four personas carried it; the advocate ranked it just below the ranked six on effect-times-prevalence but named it defensible, and no one dissented or vetoed.
open_questions: Reported OS 21.1 mo was immature at 40 events
Subsite unspecified against an intrahepatic-built indication
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate in FGFR2-fusion disease: ORR 35.5% (pmid:32203698), concordant with futibatinib in direction; single-arm surrogate endpoint.
toxicity_burden: High (grade 3+ AE 64%; hyperphosphatemia 55%, retinal detachment, hypophosphatemia)

counter_productive_moa.description: On-target FGFR inhibition; FGFR1-driven hyperphosphatemia is on-mechanism; acquired resistance mutations blunt durability.

overall: The longest-tenured FGFR2 option with the deepest safety record; edged below futibatinib on resistance-coverage sequencing, not on efficacy.
scenario_label: If FGFR2 fusion/rearrangement confirmed (RNA-based fusion panel preferred)

intervention_label: Lirafugratinib (RLY-4008), FGFR2-selective, via the ReFocus cohort (if FGFR2 fusion/rearrangement confirmed)
expected_benefit: ReFocus FGFRi-naive cohort (n=114): ORR 46.5% (95% CI 37.1-56.1), DCR 96.5%, mDoR 11.8 mo, mPFS 11.3 mo; FGFR2-selective design spares FGFR1-driven hyperphosphatemia.
key_risks: Abstract-only safety base with no registration-scale long-tail follow-up
preference_alignment: matches prefers_trials: YES (ReFocus recruiting); FGFR2-selective tolerability argument fits balanced 0.5 weight per advocate. Pre-approval status is the flagged tension.
guideline_status: Not FDA-approved and not NCCN-listed; NDA under FDA priority review, PDUFA 27 Sep 2026. Trial-enrollment lane, not a standard rec.
rationale_summary: This is the case's preference-conflict rec: the advocate and risktaker rank the FGFR2-selective agent at the head of the FGFR lane on a 46.5% ORR and the lowest hyperphosphatemia burden, arguing that under prefers_trials an enrollable next-gen agent should be surfaced, not fenced off. Three personas dissented, so per the preference-conflict rule the status is considered_with_caveats. The critic discounts abstract-only data below the peer-reviewed FGFR pivotals; the conservative names the safety datum the tolerability argument skips — grade 3+ palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia at 32.8%, which makes the selective-versus-pan-FGFR trade lateral, not a clean win; the concensusite holds that ranking a pre-approval, non-NCCN-listed agent above approved futibatinib and pemigatinib inverts the guideline order. No formal veto was issued. Provenance flag carried from the board: lirafugratinib's own basket NCT07359820 EXCLUDES cholangiocarcinoma — the 46.5% comes from the separate ReFocus cohort (NCT04526106), and the two must not be conflated.
open_questions: Full peer-reviewed paper unread; response ascertainment and censoring cannot be audited from the abstract
US access runs through the ReFocus slot or expanded access pending the September 2026 PDUFA
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate-to-high in FGFR2-fusion disease but low-certainty: ORR 46.5% (doi:10.1200/JCO.2026.44.2_suppl.476) is single-arm, abstract-only, pre-approval.

counter_productive_moa.description: FGFR2-selective on-target inhibition; critic and conservative dissented on evidence maturity and the 32.8% hand-foot burden, not a counter-productive mechanism per se.

overall: The highest-ORR FGFR2 option and the best hyperphosphatemia profile, but abstract-only, pre-approval, and carrying a one-in-three grade-3 hand-foot rate.
scenario_label: If FGFR2 fusion/rearrangement confirmed (RNA-based fusion panel preferred)

intervention_label: Zanidatamab (if HER2 IHC 3+ with reflex ISH confirmed)
expected_benefit: HERIZON-BTC-01 cohort 1 (n=80): confirmed ORR 41.3% (95% CI 30.4-52.8), mDoR 12.9 mo, mPFS 5.5 mo.
key_risks: Decreased ejection fraction 3% grade 3 (HER2 cardiac class effect) — baseline and serial echo
preference_alignment: matches balanced 0.5 weight and is placed above T-DXd on the patient's behalf on the ILD signal (no explicit veto set). IV route, but no modality constraint stated.
guideline_status: NCCN Biliary Tract Cancers v2.2025 category 2A for HER2-positive (IHC 3+) subsequent-line disease; the only dedicated biliary HER2 trial behind a guideline listing.
rationale_summary: Zanidatamab is the guideline-endorsed HER2 lead, ranked above trastuzumab deruxtecan by four personas on the strength of a dedicated biliary trial and a milder safety profile. Every persona who addressed the HER2 axis held T-DXd below zanidatamab on its 10.5% adjudicated ILD rate and three treatment-related ILD deaths in DESTINY-PanTumor02, with no pulmonary baseline or organ-function labs supplied to gate against — the conservative and advocate framed this as a shared safety downgrade of T-DXd rather than a formal veto, since no persona ranked T-DXd first. The gating test is HER2 IHC with reflex ISH on the trial's own scoring (4B5 clone), not an NGS copy-number call, so the rank-1 workup must carry the protein readout. The evidence is single-arm phase 2b behind accelerated approval, with no randomized survival comparison. HER2 skews toward extrahepatic and gallbladder disease, so a positive depends on a subsite intake never supplied.
open_questions: Subsite unspecified; HER2 prevalence hinges on it
No baseline cardiac function supplied for the 3% grade-3 ejection-fraction signal
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate in HER2-positive disease: confirmed ORR 41.3%, mDoR 12.9 mo (pmid:37276871), single-arm pivotal cohort with no randomized comparator.
toxicity_burden: Low (diarrhea 5% G3, decreased ejection fraction 3% G3, infusion reactions)

counter_productive_moa.description: On-target HER2 blockade; no mechanism-level dissent — board tension was T-DXd's ILD, resolved by ranking zanidatamab ahead.

overall: The dedicated-trial HER2 lead, ranked above T-DXd on a 10.5% ILD signal with no pulmonary baseline on file; gated on IHC 3+ with reflex ISH.
scenario_label: If HER2 IHC 3+ with reflex ISH confirmed (4B5 clone)

intervention_label: Dabrafenib + trametinib (if BRAF V600E confirmed on NGS/PCR)
expected_benefit: ROAR biliary cohort (n=43): ORR 47% (95% CI 31-62, investigator), mDoR 8.9 mo, mPFS 9.0 mo.
key_risks: Serious AE 40%; treatment-related serious AE 21% (predominantly pyrexia)
preference_alignment: matches balanced 0.5 weight; oral doublet, pyrexia manageable, no veto. Immediately actionable off the same CGP if V600E confirms.
guideline_status: NCCN Biliary Tract Cancers v2.2025 category 2A (subsequent-line) plus the tumor-agnostic FDA label.
rationale_summary: A confirmed BRAF V600E opens a doublet with cross-society and cross-label endorsement and a 47% ORR that rivals the FGFR agents. It ranks seventh on prevalence alone — V600E turns up in only 1-5% of biliary cancer and the ROAR cohort is small (n=43) and single-arm, investigator-assessed. The risktaker and concensusite both carried it in their ranked picks; no persona dissented or vetoed. The gate is a true V600E on NGS or PCR: a VE1 IHC screen alone, or a class 2/3 BRAF alteration, does not qualify. Pyrexia is the signature effect and comes with a standard dose-hold and antipyretic plan.
open_questions: Non-V600E class 2/3 BRAF alterations could be miscalled as actionable
Small single-arm basket cohort with no randomized comparator
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate-to-high in BRAF V600E disease: ORR 47%, mPFS 9.0 mo (pmid:32818466); small single-arm cohort, low prevalence caps expected yield.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (pyrexia 19%, GGT rise 12% G3+, serious AE 40%)

counter_productive_moa.description: On-target MAPK inhibition; MEK co-inhibition mitigates paradoxical RAF activation. No mechanism-level dissent raised.

overall: A high-response, dual-endorsed doublet if V600E confirms; ranked low on 1-5% prevalence and a small single-arm cohort, not on any objection.
scenario_label: If BRAF V600E confirmed on NGS or PCR (not VE1 IHC alone)

expected_benefit: DESTINY-PanTumor02 biliary cohort ORR 22% (investigator; 95% CI 10.6-37.6); IHC 3+ subgroup ORR 56.3-61.3%.
key_risks: Adjudicated drug-related ILD/pneumonitis 10.5%, with three treatment-related deaths
preference_alignment: no toxicity veto was set, so this is not a hard filter; but a balanced 0.5 weight does not reach for the ILD-risk ADC when a comparably active antibody covers the same axis. IHC 3+-only under the tumor-agnostic label.
guideline_status: Tumor-agnostic HER2 (IHC 3+) accelerated approval; basket route rather than a dedicated biliary listing. Held below zanidatamab by NCCN-aligned consensus.
rationale_summary: T-DXd is kept on the ranked list as considered-and-held-below rather than dropped, so the reader sees the HER2 option the board deliberately downgraded and why. Its IHC 3+ subgroup ORR (56-61%) is competitive with zanidatamab, but three personas dissented on the 10.5% adjudicated ILD rate and three treatment-related ILD deaths, and no pulmonary baseline, DLCO, or organ-function labs were supplied to gate the risk. The conservative flagged it as the pick most likely to draw a round-2 toxicity qualifier; because no persona ranked it above zanidatamab, the board recorded a shared downgrade, not a formal veto. Note the predictive hedge for HER2-low/expressing tumors: the tumor-agnostic approval is IHC 3+-only, so any HER2-low read is a weaker predictor and would make this investigational rather than on-label. If re-entered, it should be gated on a confirmed IHC 3+ tumor plus a baseline pulmonary assessment and a written ILD-monitoring plan; on that basis the conservative would not block it.
open_questions: No baseline pulmonary function or DLCO supplied to gate ILD risk
HER2-low expression is a weaker predictor than IHC 3+; the label does not extend to it in this setting
likelihood_of_effect: High in IHC 3+ subgroup (ORR 56-61%) but low-certainty overall: full biliary-cohort ORR 22%, investigator-assessed (pmid:37870536), gated by ILD risk.
toxicity_burden: High (ILD/pneumonitis 10.5% with 3 treatment-related deaths; grade 3+ AE 40.8%)

counter_productive_moa.description: On-mechanism ILD/pneumonitis from the deruxtecan payload can cause fatal pulmonary injury, blunting the therapeutic goal in an unmonitored patient.

overall: Competitive IHC 3+ activity held below zanidatamab on a 10.5% ILD signal with three deaths and no pulmonary baseline; re-entry needs an ILD-monitoring plan.

expected_benefit: KEYNOTE-158 MSI-H basket ORR 34.3% (95% CI 28.3-40.8), mOS 23.5 mo; TMB-high subgroup ORR 29% (95% CI 21-39) with durable responses. No CCA-specific subgroup ORR published.
key_risks: Treatment-related grade 3-5 AE 14.6% (lowest among the targeted options)
preference_alignment: matches balanced 0.5 weight (lowest grade 3+ rate); resolved by the same rank-1 workup at no added cost; serves prefers_trials. No veto.
guideline_status: Tumor-agnostic FDA labels for MSI-H/dMMR and TMB-high (>=10 mut/Mb); NCCN-endorsed for those biomarkers. KEYNOTE-158 reports no CCA-specific subgroup ORR.
rationale_summary: This is the low-prevalence, high-durability pick the advocate keeps on the ranked list because when MSI-H/dMMR lands it is durable in a way nothing else here is (mOS 23.5 mo). MSI-H runs only 1-3% in biliary cancer, so the test is most often negative, which is why it sits last. The critic and concensusite noted it as a legitimate conditional option but kept it off their ranked five on prevalence and the absence of a published CCA-specific subgroup ORR — not a dissent against the mechanism, and no veto. MMR IHC alongside the DNA panel is a cheap orthogonal check that catches cases a low-purity NGS score can miss, so both the MSI and TMB reads come off the rank-1 workup at no extra burden.
open_questions: No CCA-specific subgroup ORR published in KEYNOTE-158
TMB-high as a predictor is less tumor-type-validated than MSI-H/dMMR
likelihood_of_effect: High and durable when MSI-H/dMMR positive (ORR 34.3%, mOS 23.5 mo, pmid:31682550) but low prevalence (1-3%); TMB-high a weaker predictor.
toxicity_burden: Low (immune-mediated AEs; grade 3-5 14.6%, one treatment-related death)

counter_productive_moa.description: T-cell exhaustion is a theoretical checkpoint risk but not raised by any persona for this biomarker-selected setting.

overall: Durable benefit when MSI-H/dMMR confirms, resolved free by the rank-1 workup; ranked last on 1-3% prevalence and no published CCA subgroup ORR.
scenario_label: If MSI-H/dMMR or TMB-high (>=10 mut/Mb) confirmed
